text:
maria: quick idea — sketching a memory scheduling proto called 'Orbit' + a tiny RL-backed prefetcher to help bursty inference workloads. want to capture interface boundaries and safety limits before i write an RFC.
kevin: curious. what does Orbit buy vs our existing soft-lease/window code?
yara: short answer: tighter burst coordination + learned short-horizon prefetch hints. not trying to replace eviction policies, more like smarter admission/prefetch decisions per-request.
dmitri: so this sits between request-routing and the eviction/admission layer? basically returns hints not obligations?
maria: exactly. API idea: MemoryScheduler.offer(ctx) -> {action: "admit|defer|prefetch", hint: {pages: [...], priority}}. scheduler decides synchronously. eviction still owns residency guarantees.
maria: pseudo-config:
```yaml
orbit:
  window_ms: 150            # scheduling window for batching decisions
  cushion_pages: 6         # soft buffer to avoid immediate demote storms
  prefetch:
    model: rl-small-v0
    horizon: 3              # how many next tokens/kv-steps to predict
    max_prefetch_pct: 0.15  # max fraction of pool to prefetch
```
kevin: i like the bounded max_prefetch_pct. safety first. how do we measure bad prefetched pages (wasted work)?
yara: metric: orbit.prefetch.missed_rate = prefetched_pages_not_accessed / prefetched_pages_total. also orbit.prefetch.cpu_ms and net egress.
dmitri: rollout plan: start as purely advisory -> collect telemetry -> offline train RL -> A/B canary with fallback to LRU. minimal risk.
maria: tradeoffs:
- pro: adapt to access patterns across microbatches and session-locality, reduce tail latency spikes
- con: extra complexity, risk of mispredictions wasting memory/IO, harder reasoning about multi-tenant fairness
kevin: tenancy is big. we should never let a tenant's prefetching use more than tenant_quota * prefetch_pct. enforcement either in scheduler or lower-level quota check.
yara: interface boundary decision: scheduler must not evict or pin pages directly. only emit hints. eviction/pin API stays in residency manager. that keeps clear separation.
maria: agree. also want a simple deterministic fallback: if RL model is offline, fall back to heuristic predictor (recently used + seq distance).
dmitri: thought about training data: use anonymized per-request traces (sequence of page hits) and reward signal = reduced tail P99 tokens + net throughput per GPU-hour. need offline sim.
kevin: can we sandbox a small RL model in process? or do we call a microservice? latency matters — prefer in-proc tiny model (quantized).\ymaria-note: (ops-bot) deploy-bot: note saved: orbit-proto-discussion pinned to eng-runtime.
yara: telemetry names we need in agent: orbit.decision.latency_ms, orbit.window_utilization, orbit.prefetch.bytes, orbit.prefetch.miss_cost_ms.
maria: success criteria for canary: 5–10% reduction in P99 token latency on selected workloads, prefetch_miss_rate < 0.25, no >2% increase in overall bandwidth cost.
kevin: action items: I'll prototype MemoryScheduler interface in runtime (PR + smoke harness). maria: you'll sketch training pipeline and simulator. yara: add telemetry spec and dashboard. dmitri: think through multi-tenant quota enforcement.
maria: awesome. i'll draft a short RFC after we have a prototype and some sim numbers.
yara: small note — ensure we expose debug traces per request (flags) so canary can inspect decisions.
dmitri: also add a kill switch in console per node and a global opt-out for customers who need deterministic behavior.
maria: cool. leaving the thread to capture more comments. if anyone has objections to the interface boundary (hints-only) shout now. :eyes:
